title: MLflow release versioning: bump Python, Java, R, docs, and UI version strings together; Helm appVersion tracks the last released version
answers: Where is the MLflow version number defined, and which files must change when bumping it after a release?
Why does the Helm chart appVersion lag the dev version in charts/Chart.yaml?
I need to change the package version for mlflow-skinny or mlflow-tracing; what else has to match?
Why does the UI or docs show a different version than the Python package after a release?
body:
Path: Version strings for every MLflow artifact are set in several places: Python via mlflow/version.py:VERSION and the pyproject.toml files (pyproject.toml, pyproject.release.toml, libs/skinny/pyproject.toml, libs/tracing/pyproject.toml); Java via mlflow/java/pom.xml and the spark_2.12/spark_2.13/client poms (SNAPSHOT form); R via mlflow/R/mlflow/DESCRIPTION; UI via mlflow/server/js/src/common/constants.tsx:Version; docs via docs/src/constants.ts:Version; Helm via charts/Chart.yaml appVersion.
Rule: After a release, move all dev-version locations together to the next development version (e.g. 3.16.2.dev0 in Python/UI/docs, 3.16.2-SNAPSHOT in Java, 3.16.2 in R). Keep the pyproject.release.toml pins for mlflow-skinny and mlflow-tracing identical to the new mlflow version. Helm charts/Chart.yaml appVersion is set to the last released version (3.16.1), not the dev version.
Symptom: (omit for conventions)
Constraints: Applies to version bumps only. Not the place for changing dependency ranges. Only the editable mlflow entry in uv.lock is updated for the bump, per the PR description; do not regenerate the full lockfile in a version bump. A test under tests/dev and tests/test_version.py covers version consistency per the PR description.
applies: Repository-wide release/version bump work for MLflow packages, UI, docs, Java, R, and Helm chart.
says: The web interface displays an outdated version number after our latest software release.
Documentation pages show a different release version than the newly installed application package.
The Kubernetes deployment template should reference the latest official release rather than development builds.
Synchronize version numbers across the user interface, documentation, and client libraries after release.
search: Repository version bumps across Python (mlflow/version.py:VERSION, pyproject.toml, pyproject.release.toml, libs/*/pyproject.toml), Java pom.xml files, R DESCRIPTION, UI constants, and docs constants must be updated together to the next development version. Helm chart appVersion in charts/Chart.yaml must track the last released version rather than the development version, and pyproject.release.toml pins for mlflow-skinny and mlflow-tracing must match the new version. Only the editable mlflow entry in uv.lock should be updated, without regenerating the full lockfile or changing dependency ranges.
